description: Rules from spec/90-extensions/semver.md: the opt-in SemVer 2.0.0 bridge (SEM-1..SEM-5, SEM-7). Every vector names the bridge it exercises (CON-28), so an implementation that does not claim it skips them.

vectors.name: semver/claim-must-be-an-object
vectors.description: The claim is an object; a boolean says nothing about what was claimed.

vectors.name: semver/claim-requires-the-scheme
vectors.description: Claiming the SemVer bridge on a record whose scheme is not semver contradicts itself.

vectors.name: semver/version-rejects-a-tag-prefix
vectors.description: 'v1.4.2' is a tag, which SemVer's own FAQ distinguishes from a version.

vectors.name: semver/version-rejects-a-partial-version
vectors.description: A SemVer version has three numbers; '1.4' is not one.

vectors.name: semver/version-rejects-a-range
vectors.description: A range belongs to a package manager, not to SemVer; the record carries one version.

vectors.name: semver/version-rejects-whitespace
vectors.description: Whitespace is not part of the grammar, and trimming would be a normalisation (SCH-7).

vectors.name: semver/version-rejects-a-trailing-newline
vectors.description: A regex end anchor may match before a newline; the grammar must consume the whole value, so '1.4.2\n' is not a version.

vectors.name: semver/version-rejects-a-leading-zero
vectors.description: '1.04.2' violates the numeric-identifier rule; accepting it would make two strings compare differently than they look.

vectors.name: semver/version-accepts-prerelease-and-build
vectors.description: A prerelease with build metadata is a full SemVer version and is carried verbatim.

vectors.name: semver/version-accepts-zero
vectors.description: Zero is a version; a project that starts at 0.0.0 is not doing anything wrong.

vectors.name: semver/sequence-is-forbidden
vectors.description: SemVer defines the order; a second ordering in scheme.sequence could contradict it (SCH-8).

vectors.name: semver/tag-must-carry-the-version
vectors.description: A tag naming a different version contradicts the version it sits next to.

vectors.name: semver/tag-rejects-whitespace
vectors.description: Git refs cannot contain spaces; a 'tag' that does is not a tag.

vectors.name: semver/tag-accepts-a-project-prefix
vectors.description: Monorepo tags name the package before the version; the prefix is project policy and is preserved.

vectors.name: semver/tag-omits-build-metadata
vectors.description: A tag may carry the precedence part while the version carries build metadata; the tag still matches.

vectors.name: semver/authority-is-only-recommended
vectors.description: A missing authority is a warning, not a rejection (ADR-0005): the record still conforms.

vectors.name: semver/empty-claim-is-accepted
vectors.description: The claim object may be empty when the project publishes no tag to map.

vectors.name: semver/unclaimed-record-stays-opaque
vectors.description: Without the claim, 'semver' is just a scheme name and the label stays opaque (SCH-7); no bridge rule applies, and no bridge implementation is needed to pass this vector.
